clue.text: Stranger from France reorganised IKEA on return

indicators.note: reorganised says the letters of IKEA are put into a new order
return asks for the word meaning 'on' to be read backwards

parts.note: on means 'regarding', which is RE

explanation.surface: Something odd from France: a flat-pack store rearranged on its way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reorganised' turns IKEA into EAKI; 'return' turns RE into ER. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranger as a comparative adjective means more unusual, and freakier is a comparative meaning the same.

clue.text: Aim at spot at centre of token

parts.note: to spot something is to see it

indicators.note: at centre of asks for the middle letter of the word token

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hit the spot at the centre of a token, like a target.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek something is to try for it, to aim at it as a goal.

clue.text: Surgical procedure means life and beginnings of prodigious sex — yes!

parts.note: BIO is a short form meaning life, as in biology

indicators.note: beginnings of asks for the first letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic exclamation about a life of prodigious sex, oddly passed off as a surgical procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A biopsy is a medical operation in which tissue is removed for examination.

clue.text: Hair transplant claim involving setters?

indicators.note: involving says one piece is wrapped around the other
transplant says the letters of claim are moved into a new arrangement

parts.note: setters, speaking of themselves, are US

explanation.surface: A hair transplant claim that seems to involve hairdressers who set hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transplant' makes MICAL, which 'involving' wraps round US. Hair looks like hair on a head; it is the 1960s stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair is a famous rock musical of the 1960s, so it is an example of the genre.

clue.text: Asiatic cooks taking cocaine for painful condition

indicators.note: taking says the anagram takes in another letter
cooks in the sense of falsifies or rearranges, so the letters of Asiatic are reordered

parts.note: C is a slang abbreviation for cocaine

explanation.surface: Asian chefs on cocaine end up with a painful condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooks' rearranges ASIATIC as SIATICA, and 'taking' puts C inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sciatica is pain along the sciatic nerve in the back and leg, a painful ailment.

clue.text: Disparaging term for a medium asteroid orbiting round America

indicators.note: round says one piece goes around the other
orbiting suggests going round and round, so the letters of asteroid are shuffled

explanation.surface: An astronomer's line about an asteroid circling the Americas, apparently a slur on a psychic medium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orbiting' makes STERADIO, which 'round' wraps around the abbreviation. 'Medium' suggests a psychic; it is a broadcasting medium.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam radio was a mocking name, after television arrived, for sound broadcasting as old-fashioned.

clue.text: Rockers possibly making church appearances

parts.note: airs are manners or appearances put on

explanation.surface: Rock musicians, perhaps, turning up in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rockers' suggests rock musicians, but rocking chairs are meant; 'possibly' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocking chair is one kind of seat, so rockers are examples of seating.

clue.text: A basis for prayers

parts.note: read literally, the thing at the base of praying: a kneeling desk on which someone at prayer rests

explanation.walkthrough: The French name means 'pray God'; it is a low desk with a ledge for kneeling and a rest for a book.
explanation.definitionFit: This piece of furniture is literally what a worshipper kneels on and leans on while praying.

clue.text: Round bag

definitions.meaning: a type of round, a song sung in overlapping parts

explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a musical round, and to bag an animal or prize is to capture it.

clue.text: Sailor Bill opens two consecutive letters

indicators.note: opens says one piece breaks into the other, splitting it open

parts.note: J and K follow each other in the alphabet
AC is an abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A sailor named Bill opening a pair of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sailor Bill' reads as one man; Bill is the wordplay. Jack, or Jack Tar, is old slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Tar was traditional slang for a seaman, so jack is a crossword sailor.

clue.text: At first sight, a campfire's about to engulf one

indicators.note: to engulf says the anagram swallows another letter
about here means 'around in a jumble', so the letters of a campfire are rearranged

parts.note: the words a campfire supply the letters to rearrange; the 's is a link meaning 'is'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: From first glance a campfire looks ready to swallow someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges A CAMPFIRE, and 'to engulf' puts I inside; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prima facie is Latin for on the face of it, used for something accepted at first view.

clue.text: Neatly replacing one with daughter, Merry

indicators.note: replacing ... with says one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: neatly means tidily
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A happy daughter takes over a job neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the I's in TIDILY becomes D. Tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Merry is a gentle word for tipsy, and tiddly is British slang for the same slightly drunk state.

clue.text: Astute, missing nothing, considering disorder

indicators.note: disorder says the letters of considering are thrown into a new order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A shrewd mind, missing nothing, weighs up the chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes O from CONSIDERING; 'disorder' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An astute person is perceptive and shrewd, showing good judgement, which is what discerning means.

clue.text: Keeper likely to get a buzz from a new strip to go over international one

definitions.text: Keeper likely to get a buzz

indicators.note: to go over says the anagram covers, surrounding, the next pieces
new says the letters of strip are made into something new

parts.note: A means one, as in 'a thing'

explanation.surface: A sports keeper thrilled by a new kit going over the international one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges STRIP as PRIST, and 'to go over' puts it around IA.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper is surrounded by buzzing insects, so this keeper is apt to be buzzed.

clue.text: Put out drugs for trials

parts.note: someone put out is annoyed, cross
E is slang for the drug ecstasy, so ES are drugs

explanation.surface: Annoyed by drugs used in trials.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosses to bear are burdens or ordeals, so crosses are trials in the sense of afflictions.

clue.text: Placed in centre pile: 'Psychological Recurring Attacks'

indicators.note: placed in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Reads as a magazine headline about psychology filed in the middle of the heap.
explanation.definitionFit: Epilepsy is a neurological disorder marked by repeated seizures, which are fits or attacks.

clue.text: In the outskirts of Los Angeles, snake passes for fish?

indicators.note: In says the following piece goes inside the outskirts
the outskirts of asks for the outer letters of Los Angeles

parts.note: an adder is a snake

explanation.surface: A snake slithers on the edge of LA, passing for a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake passes' recalls Snakes and Ladders; here a fish ladder is a stepped channel letting fish pass a dam.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish ladders are series of pools built so migrating fish can get past weirs and dams.

clue.text: X-ray unit or back specialist hospital department's information

indicators.note: back says the word or is read in reverse

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An X-ray, or a back specialist's report from a hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns OR into RO. Gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: The roentgen is an old unit measuring exposure to ionising radiation such as X-rays.

clue.text: 2 in 100 Poles have a duty to go inside

indicators.note: to go inside says this piece is placed within the other

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles
ought means to have a duty

explanation.surface: Two in a hundred Poles are obliged to stay indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: '2 in 100' reads as a statistic; the 100 is written with two zeros.
explanation.definitionFit: Noughts are zeros, and the figure 100 contains two of them.

clue.text: Infection of one's darling — getting one shot

parts.note: one's read as 'one is' gives I'M
a pet is a darling, a favourite
I is the Roman numeral one
a shot is a go, an attempt

explanation.surface: A sweetheart's infection is caught with a single injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests an injection but means a try.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetigo is a contagious bacterial skin infection, common in children.

clue.text: Native American doctor, one who favours war

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
a hawk is someone who favours military action

explanation.surface: A Native American doctor with warlike views.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohawk are a Native American people of the Iroquois confederacy.

clue.text: Rock group members' initially short tempers

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of the word short

parts.note: to temper something is to tone it down, so tempers means tones

explanation.surface: Band members known for their short tempers.
explanation.walkthrough: Members of the Rolling Stones are Stones; the apostrophe makes the definition possessive, and the answer reads that way too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rolling Stones are often just called the Stones, so a member of the band is a Stone.

clue.text: Treacherous types: racers, perhaps

definitions.meaning: ... in the grass are treacherous people
racers are a family of fast American ..., so they are examples

explanation.definitionFit: A snake is figuratively a deceitful person, and the racer is a real serpent species.

clue.text: Black-eyed Susan, environmental activist and international ace

parts.note: Greta Thunberg is the Swedish climate campaigner
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A woman called Susan with a black eye, alongside a campaigner and a star player.
explanation.definitionFit: Black-eyed Susan is the common name for Thunbergia alata, a climbing plant with dark-centred flowers.

clue.text: Has old bowler possibly arrived at end of pitch?

parts.note: a bowler is one kind of hat

indicators.note: end of asks for the last letter of the word pitch

explanation.surface: A cricket question: has the old bowler reached the far end of the pitch?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket; a bowler is also a hat. Cricket's bowler delivers the ball down the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Hath is the archaic third-person form of the verb to have, so it means has in old English.

clue.text: Said to be a conflicted character's mask

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken and the answer is its sound-alike

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the evil side of Dr Jekyll's split personality

explanation.surface: A torn character's mask, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: Jekyll and Hyde, from Stevenson's story, are one man's two selves.
explanation.definitionFit: To mask something is to conceal it, and to hide is to conceal.

clue.text: Wife is a printer? Shows she's not being serious

parts.note: a printer is one who inks paper, so the phrase gives inks

explanation.surface: Is his wife a printer? Her signal makes plain she's joking.
explanation.definitionFit: A wink is a playful facial signal that something is said in jest.

clue.text: Dodgy dealer goes in back way for sewing machine parts

indicators.note: goes in says the anagram is placed inside the other piece
back says the abbreviation for way is read in reverse

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: dodgy suggests something not straight, so the letters of dealer are jumbled

explanation.surface: A shady dealer slips in by a rear entrance to get parts for sewing machines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' makes READLE and 'back' makes TS; 'goes in' puts the first inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Treadles are foot pedals that drive old sewing machines and looms.
